notes: Web 419 — NAV-ML-LEARNING stage 1 (Nov 11, 2026). Owner (Nov 10): the Navigator must be dynamic, learning each trucker's own route choices — a road too small, traffic building up, or plain gut feel — instead of always spitting out the same router route. Stage 1 lives in the new js/navlearn.js with five small hooks in the Navigator: (1) ROUTE CAPTURE — while a drive runs, the path actually driven is recorded off the existing fix stream, thinned to ≥25 m points; automatic, no taps, no new UI anywhere. (2) DEVIATION LEARNING — a drive teaches only when it completes (its trace ends within 250 m of the destination after ≥400 m and ≥8 points); when more than a quarter of its points ran more than 75 m off the route the Navigator suggested for that origin→destination pair (pairs keyed by ~150 m cells, the same grid as the load counter's site profiles), the driven path is stored as the pair's learned route with a drive count: one drive plants it, a repeat deviation refreshes it with the newest way, and a drive completed ON the learned route adds to the count while keeping the stored line. A drive that follows the suggested route, or ends anywhere but at the destination, teaches nothing. (3) LEARNED ROUTE OFFERED — doRoute consults the learned store before asking the server (never mid-drive, never over a split-shift plan, never for a destination whose learned route was left earlier that drive): the adopted route is his own driven line under a two-maneuver plan whose time is his own average over that pair's drives, and the route summary carries one quiet line — 'Your usual route — learned from your driving · driven N times'. Leaving a learned route behaves exactly like leaving any route: the off-route re-route is the standard router's, the learned route stays suppressed for that destination for the rest of the drive, and such a hybrid drive neither strengthens the learned route nor teaches a new one. (4) PER-USER — the store key 'navlearn_routes' rides the ordinary App._store → Firestore mirror, like the load counter's 'geoload_site_profiles': this account's learning, from this driver's own driving only. A fresh account has no learned routes and routes exactly as before this build. Learned routes are client-side data — no trace goes to the nav server beyond what routing already sends. Deliberately NOT in stage 1: traffic-aware learning, road-size learning from other drivers, and named-road turn guidance along a learned line (the learned plan carries the line, the distance and his typical time; the voice names it as his usual route). Bench: tools/nav-ml-learning-stage1-test.js 34/34 — plant / refresh / strengthen, the third navigation of a pair offered the learned path with his average ETA, fresh profile empty, followed / abandoned / too-short drives teach nothing, ~150 m cell keying, thinning, and the hooks + suppression wired with no new UI. Neighbours: navigator-v135 95/95, nav-v260 24/24, dispatch-navnotes-v414 30/30; the navigator-test / navigator-screen / nav-2step failure sets are byte-identical to pristine 418 (pre-existing). Verdict owed in his hands: drive a pair his own way twice, then navigate it again and watch his own route come up first, with the quiet line naming it.
